input.rationale: The fee articles (Article V user-fee tiers, Supplemental Payments, rebate shares) contain no best-price or best-terms undertaking by Licensee, so pricing is clean. The one MFN-family obligation burdening us is Article XXII: we must disclose any bona fide third-party offer for our assets or control and then afford Licensor a right to take that transaction on the same terms — a right-to-match/most-favoured-offer mechanic running in Vendor's favour. It is not limited to a defined product, runs for the entire term (36 months plus extensions, far beyond 12 months) and has no like-for-like comparison carve-outs, so it fails every fallback element and sits in walk-away territory as an open-ended obligation to extend Licensor the terms offered to a third party. We therefore take the preferred position and strike the mechanic, conforming the surviving sentence so no orphan reference to the deleted "Right of First Refusal" or "Exercise Period" remains.

mappings.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.

proposal.summary: Strike the Licensor right of first refusal / right-to-match and conform the surviving sentence
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have struck Article XXII because it obliges us to disclose any bona fide third-party offer and to offer Licensor the same transaction terms for the entire term, and our playbook accepts no most-favoured-nation or right-to-match obligation benefiting the Vendor. We conformed the following sentence so it reads as a clean confirmation of our right to proceed and leaves no reference to the deleted mechanic.

ops.oldText: ARTICLE XXII RIGHT OF FIRST REFUSAL During the term of this Agreement, the Licensor shall have the right (the "Right of First Refusal"), for a period (the "Exercise Period") expiring at 11:59 PM (Eastern Time) on the fifth (5th) business day after the giving of written notice by the Licensee that it has received a bonafide offer from a third party to (ii) purchase all or substantially all of the assets of Licensee; or (ii) to engage in a merger or consolidation in which Licensee is not the surviving corporation or in which, if Licensee is the surviving corporation, the owners of Licensee immediately prior to the consummation of such merger or consolidation do not, immediately after consummation of such merger or consolidation, own stock or other securities of Licensee that possess a majority of the voting power of all Licensee's outstanding stock and other securities and the power to elect a majority of the members of Licensee's board of directors.
